name: Parawen
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang district New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU (hdl 1885/130077).
tone_statements.quote: 2 . 22 . 8 . 1 . Tlp o lo gi c a l Ch ar a c t e r i s t i c s o f t h e Ade lb e rt Ran ge Phy lum … Th e aim o f th i s s e c t i on i s t o p o in t o u t s ome o f t h e t yp o l o gi c a l fe at ure s wh i ch are uni - ve r s a l ly o r a lmo s t uni ve rs a l ly p r e s e nt in t h e l anguage s o f t h e Phy lum . 1) Th e ve lar nas al i s very c ommon . 2) N one o f the l angu age s app e ar s t o b e t on a l .
tone_statements.locator: p. 135, sec. 2.22.8.1 'Typological Characteristics of the Adelbert Range Phylum', item 2 (normalised: 'None of the languages appears to be tonal.')
tone_statements.summary: Survey judgement that no Adelbert Range Phylum language, Parawen included, appears to be tonal; no tone analysis or inventory; stress not marked because stress patterning was not yet established.

sources.note: Only source Z'graggen (1980); retyped lexicon without stress marks.
Phoneme tables copied from Pick 2020 p. 158; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 485 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 4.4 'Parawen' (pp. 157-158) gives only a phoneme inventory (/i u a/; /b t d k g m n w y/), allophony and final-vowel epenthesis, 'based solely on the phonetic transcriptions of Z'graggen's wordlists, so.. extremely tentative' (fn. 10, p. 31); nothing on stress. Sec. 1.5.1 'Stress' (pp. 31-32): stress described only for Mauwake, Pamosu, Usan; 'Unfortunately, the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'. Sec. 10.6 (p. 425) Parawen sound changes: nothing on stress.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG 'PNG Language Resources: Parawen' (Internet Archive copy 2015)
sources.note: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' -- no SIL description exists.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU. (Parawen = F19)
sources.note: Intro sec. 7 (pp. viii-ix): 'The transcription is rendered semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; no Parawen entry in the fluctuation table; no statement on stress; Parawen forms (e.g. p. 20 = p. 36, 'throat' marimana) carry vowel-length marks but no stress marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38, 569-612.
sources.note: Population figure (F19 Parawen 432) and comparative lexical rows only; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (Parawen = language 33, Wayapan Family/Group, Pihom Stock)
sources.note: Sec. 2.22.24 (pp. 53-54): villages, cognate percentages, segmental notes (/k/ and a velar fricative observed in Parawen; r/l not contrastive in Parawen); sec. 2.22.27 Pihom Stock typology (p. 55): segmental only; sec. 2.22.8 Adelbert Range Phylum (p. 73): 'None of the languages appears to be tonal.' No statement on stress anywhere.

sources.citation: Any future SIL-PNG survey report / Organised Phonology Data for Parawen [prw] (none listed by SIL-PNG as of the 2015 capture or by OLAC).
